Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) of tumor immune microenvironment composition identifies four robust patient subtypes in the NSCLC anti-PD-1 atlas (GSE243013, n=242 patients), and these subtypes are significantly associated with pathological response to anti-PD-1 therapy (chi-squared p=0.0042).

The four immune subtypes and their response profiles:

1. B-cell-enriched subtype (n=86, 35.5%): Dominated by memory B cells (Bm_PDE4D, Bm_TNFSF9, Bm_TNF). Significantly higher response rate: 67.4% responders (OR=2.42, p=0.0019). This is the optimal subtype for anti-PD-1 benefit, consistent with the known role of B cells and tertiary lymphoid structures in immunotherapy response.

2. T-cell-enriched subtype (n=89, 36.8%): High CD8+ memory/effector T cells (CD8T_Tm_IL7R, CD8T_Tem_GZMK+GZMH+). Intermediate response rate: 48.3% (OR=0.71, p=0.23, ns). T-cell infiltration alone does not guarantee response.

3. Myeloid-enriched subtype (n=33, 13.6%): High macrophages (Mφ_MARCO, Mφ_VCAN). Response rate: 60.6% (OR=1.39, p=0.45, ns). Above-average response despite macrophage dominance.

4. Plasma/Treg-enriched subtype (n=34, 14.0%): High plasma cells and regulatory T cells (Plasma_cell, CD4T_Treg_FOXP3, CD4T_Treg_CCR8). Significantly lower response rate: 26.5% (OR=0.26, p=0.0007). This is the poorest-prognosis subtype, where concurrent Treg infiltration likely suppresses anti-tumor immunity.

The continuous NMF component weights confirm these findings: higher B-cell component weight is the strongest predictor of response (logistic regression coef=5.10, p=1.5×10⁻⁷), while higher plasma/Treg component weight predicts resistance (coef relative to Component 3 reference: all other components have significantly positive coefficients). These associations remain significant after adjusting for age, gender, smoking, and cancer type.

The NMF-based classification is not confounded by cancer type (p=0.87), gender, or smoking history, confirming that the immune subtypes represent genuine biological variation in the tumor microenvironment rather than clinical demographics.

Optimal number of components: k=4, selected by reconstruction error elbow analysis (reconstruction error: 1.987; consensus stability across 20 random restarts: cophenetic correlation = 1.0 for all k tested, indicating robust structure). PCA on the same data explained only 55.2% cumulative variance with the first 4 components and produced less interpretable components, supporting NMF as the preferred method for this analysis.
